title: Anal fissure treatment
what: The doctor examines the tear at the anus and chooses treatment. Usually it is ointments, diet, and warm baths, sometimes a small procedure.
why: For pain and blood during or after going to the toilet.
duration: the visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; with treatment, healing usually takes a few weeks
tell_doctor: How long it has hurt, and if there is blood
If you have constipation or diarrhea
If you are pregnant or recently gave birth

prepare.title: Bowels
prepare.text: You usually do not need a bowel prep. If a procedure is planned, check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Wash with warm water in the morning.

prepare.title: Pain
prepare.text: If it hurts a lot, the doctor will examine you very gently. Tell them.

steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
You lie on your side with your knees bent
The doctor looks at the area around the anus
If it is very painful, a deeper exam may be postponed
The doctor prescribes treatment and explains how to use it
If ointments do not help, an injection or small surgery may be offered
feel: The exam may be painful. The doctor will be careful
It may feel awkward. It is a routine topic for a doctor
after: Eat more vegetables and fruit, and drink water. Your stool should be soft
Warm sitz baths as your doctor advises
Use only the ointments and suppositories your doctor prescribed
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) with growing pain or swelling at the anus

faq.q: Will the fissure heal without surgery?
faq.a: Often yes, with treatment and soft stools. Surgery is needed if treatment does not work.

faq.q: Why does going to the toilet hurt so much?
faq.a: The tear gets irritated, and the muscle tightens in a spasm. Treatment relieves the spasm and pain.

reminders.text: Fissure appointment tomorrow. Wash with warm water in the morning, and bring your medicine list.
